01

Programme portfolio

Next semester activity planning

Confirm which activities the club must deliver, which proposals merit a controlled pilot and when each activity should occur.

Compulsory programme

  • Recruitment Drive: retain as a compulsory activity and connect recruitment messages with the next semester’s class offer.
  • Weekly yoga classes: retain as the club’s core recurring activity, supported by attendance evidence and a defined certification policy.
  • Free yoga classes: retain as a compulsory access and recruitment activity. The committee must determine how the free-class offer relates to first-time participants.

Long-semester practice capacity

Plan approximately six to eight practical sessions in addition to regular classes. These sessions may extend certification hours and provide supervised training opportunities for student coaches. Scheduling should use common student free hours rather than assume a single cohort’s availability.

Optional activities requiring a decision

Members’ Night: assess it as a reward for members who attend weekly classes regularly. Clarify eligibility before publicity begins.

Meditation: test one or two selected sessions rather than immediately establishing a weekly programme. Decide whether the pilot will be free or paid.

Natural Yoga: decide whether the pilot belongs in the coming semester or should move to February 2027. Confirm programme definition, facilitator and resource requirements.

Decision to recordConfirmed activity list, provisional frequency, semester timing, responsible department and proposal due date.
02

Participation and growth

October Recruitment Drive planning and promotion

Approve a credible recruitment offer and ensure that Publicity communicates only benefits that the committee and Treasurer have confirmed.

Promotion proposition

  • Present club merchandise and any confirmed lucky draw activity.
  • Explain weekly-class certification in terms that match the final attendance policy.
  • If confirmed, introduce Members’ Night after the October free class.
  • Possible Members’ Night benefits include food, health-oriented gifts, participant feedback activities and information about upcoming classes.

Participant offers and recruitment

  • Review whether a first-time participant may attend one class without charge.
  • Assess a fee waiver for members who bring new participants to selected classes. Define eligibility and financial limits before promotion.
  • Include recruitment for the vacant Vice Treasurer position in the Recruitment Drive message.
  • Assign responsibility for a follow-up survey covering participant experience, interest in future classes and membership intent.
Questions that must be resolved before publication

Offer: Who qualifies as a first-time participant, and does the free class apply once per person?

Referral: Which classes permit a fee waiver, and what evidence shows that the member brought a new participant?

Benefits: Which merchandise, food or gifts have budget approval?

Survey: Who owns the form, distribution, analysis and reporting?

Decision to recordRecruitment offer, benefit wording, target audience, survey owner, vacancy message and approval deadline for publicity.
03

Documentation and accountability

Secretarial proposals and semester reports

Establish a complete document-control system so that no proposal, minute, approval or semester report is omitted.

Proposal standard

Prepare one proposal for each event or activity where institutional requirements apply. Every proposal should contain enough information for review and later reporting.

  • Event details and objectives
  • Schedule and venue
  • Budget and financial arrangements
  • Publicity and registration process
  • Approval requirements and submission timeline

Submit each required proposal before the activity takes place and within the applicable approval timeline.

Semester report coverage by Week 14

  • Weekly yoga classes
  • Recruitment Drive
  • EXCO Meeting 1 and EXCO Meeting 2
  • Free yoga class
  • Office Bearers
  • Any additional activity, event, meeting or matter requiring a formal report
Traceability and checklist requirements

Master checklist
Track document title, activity, owner, status, due date, submission date and approval outcome.

Participation evidence
Improve attendance records so the club can verify weekly-class participation and certificate eligibility.

Service evidence
Record student coach hours and roles in a form that supports accountability and service certification.

Decision to recordChecklist format, document owners, Week 14 review schedule, attendance method and authoritative storage location.

Financial governance

Treasury policy for classes and events

Define how financial decisions become verified event information, public pricing and auditable records.

1

Treasurer

Prepares the event policy, price, benefit conditions, budget and supporting documents.

2

Secretary

Records confirmed financial arrangements in proposals, reports and the central document checklist.

3

Publicity

Publishes pricing, payment and benefit information only after verification.

Minimum financial record

  • Approved budget or funding limit
  • Supplier quotation or price basis where applicable
  • Participant pricing and member benefits
  • Receipts, payment evidence and reconciliation
  • Any refund, waiver or exception decision

Website functions

Simple fee tracking and unified receipt uploading have already been prepared in the proposed Yoga Club website. They are not urgent, but the committee should define when they become the authoritative record and who may access financial evidence.

A digital tool does not replace a policy. Confirm responsibility, access and verification before relying on it.

Decision to recordRequired documents, approval authority, verification sequence, financial-record owner and conditions for using the website.
05

Capability and recognition

Student Instructor Programme and certification guide

Agree who may enter the programme, what benefit applies and which people have authority to certify participation.

Entry requirement

Route A

More than two semester-based Certificates of Completion for weekly yoga classes.

or Route B

One yearly Certificate of Completion if the club adopts the yearly certification system.

Semester-based certificates apply only to long semesters of approximately fourteen weeks.

Benefit and signing authority

Fee-waiver proposal: consider a waiver for student instructors who maintain more than 80 per cent class attendance. Clarify the qualifying period, financial effect and whether the benefit applies before or after service.

Proposed signatories: Instructor Ms Chew, the Yoga Club Auditor, the Yoga Club Chairperson, and Ms Belinda, Ms Heng or a Core Advisor. Confirm the required combination rather than assuming every listed person must sign.

Evidence needed for a defensible decision

Which attendance record establishes the 80 per cent threshold?

How will the club recognise certificates from different semesters?

Who verifies instructor eligibility before assignment?

Which signatories have formal institutional authority?

Decision to recordEligibility route, evidence source, fee-waiver rule, authorised signatory combination and certificate-approval process.

Programme coverage

Verification before publication

Publicity archive

07

Participation evidence

Weekly class certification policy

Select a certification model that participants can understand and the club can verify consistently through attendance records.

Semester model

80%

Minimum proposed attendance for a Certificate of Completion (结业证书), based on approximately fourteen hours or fourteen class days in a long semester.

Attendance from a short semester may accumulate towards the long-semester requirement.

Yearly alternative

35

Approximately thirty-five hours, thirty-five days or thirty-five yoga practice classes.

The committee must choose one measurable unit and define how classes of different duration count.

Proposed signatories

Instructor Ms Chew, Student Coach HOD Ms Xinle, the Yoga Club Chairperson, and Ms Belinda, Ms Heng or a Core Advisor. Confirm the required combination and signing sequence.

Certificate identity

Confirm the number and type of logos permitted on the certificate. Potential marks include the Yoga Club, DSA and UTAR logos where approval permits their use.

Decision to recordCertification model, measurement unit, attendance evidence, treatment of short semesters, signatories and permitted logos.
08

Committee capacity

Higher committee recruitment

Fill leadership and publicity gaps early enough for new members to understand their responsibilities before the semester begins.

Priority recruitment

Vice Chairperson: identify a suitable current committee member with a strong student network and the capacity to support cross-department coordination.

Publicity: recruit one additional team member to support the expanded programme and reduce dependence on a single contributor.

Higher committee: recruit additional members where workload, succession or continuity risk justifies the appointment.

Candidate routes and assessment

  • Committee members may invite suitable friends or students to express interest.
  • Consider EA recruitment for experience-based roles connected with student instruction, committee participation, event support or publicity.
  • Assess availability, reliability, role understanding and willingness to maintain required records.
  • Use personal networks to identify candidates, while applying consistent role criteria.
Onboarding expectations

Role clarity
Provide a written scope and reporting relationship.

Handover
Give access to current files, deadlines and approval routes.

Commitment
Confirm availability before allocating critical work.

Decision to recordVacancies, candidate criteria, recruitment owner, communication channel, selection date and onboarding responsibility.

Member proposition

New Yoga Club merchandise

Reduce the initial idea set to a commercially feasible shortlist before design, supplier quotation and pre-funding decisions.

Higher-end

Logo cape or cloak, yoga mat, yoga bricks

Middle-range

Yoga brick, T-shirt, hat, stretching strap

Lower-cost

Keychain, lanyard, rubber wristband and other suitable small items

Selection and delivery process

Every committee member should participate in the merchandise poll and select at least three preferred items from the limited choices. Publicity develops designs for the approved shortlist. The Secretary includes selected merchandise in the proposal. The Treasurer reviews supplier pricing, minimum order quantities, pre-funding and budget implications before confirmation.

Decision to recordPolling deadline, shortlist size, selection criteria, design owner, quotation requirements and provisional budget ceiling.
10

Recognition and retention

Members’ Night and lucky draw

Determine whether the proposed activity offers a fair, affordable and clearly governed form of member recognition.

Intended audience and purpose

The activity may recognise participants who attended the June weekly classes and welcome new members joining the club. The committee should clarify whether eligibility depends on attendance history, current membership, October registration or a combination of these factors.

Link the event to participation and retention rather than treat it as an isolated social activity.

Possible benefits

  • Free food or health-oriented gifts
  • Selected club merchandise in the lucky draw pool
  • Participant feedback and recognition
  • Promotion of upcoming yoga classes
Budget and fairness conditions

Funding: club funding requires budget review and approval before commitment.

Eligibility: state the rules before members act in reliance on them.

Selection: document how lucky draw entries and winners are determined.

Evidence: retain purchasing and distribution records for funded items.

Decision to recordGo or no-go decision, eligibility, benefits, draw method, provisional budget, approval authority and event owner.

A new idea should enter the action register only when the committee can state its purpose, accountable owner, next decision point and required approval. Ideas requiring investigation may remain provisional, but they still need a return date and named person responsible for bringing evidence back to the EXCO.
